competitive_landscape: Penghu is served today by conventional inter-island and mainland ferries plus a heavy reliance on Uni Air and Mandarin Airlines. The reason air carries so much of the load is precisely the sea crossing's slowness and weather-fragility — strong evidence of latent marine demand that a fast, reliable foiling network can convert. The diesel ferries are the status quo to improve on, not a rival.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Runs the whole intra-archipelago network — Magong↔Jibei/Wangan/Cimei and the short ~25 nm Budai (Chiayi) mainland gateway — all inside the 70 nm all-electric range, on the calm inner sea where foiling smoothness directly counters the strait's wind.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries the long open-strait line to Kaohsiung (~75 nm), beyond the all-electric envelope, where the hybrid range and refuel-anywhere model deliver the all-weather reliability that the exposed Taiwan Strait demands.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proves a phased clean-foiling network works across a weather-exposed, multi-island geography — the model for an archipelago like Penghu.

regulatory_note: Operations sit under Penghu County, the Penghu National Scenic Area Administration (Tourism Administration, MOTC) and the Taiwan International Ports Corporation (Magong sub-port), with the MOTC Maritime and Port Bureau on national rules. Penghu's pursuit of UNESCO Biosphere Reserve recognition makes a zero-local-emission, low-wake foiling fleet a natural fit for its conservation positioning. Keep all framing to domestic Taiwan waters and recognised mainland gateways (Chiayi/Budai, Kaohsiung).
seasonality: Penghu sits in one of the windiest seas in the region: a powerful winter NE monsoon (roughly Oct–Mar) and the summer typhoon season bracket the year, and even summer afternoons can blow hard across the strait. This weather-fragility is the core demand hook — foiling above the surface holds a smoother, more reliable ride exactly when conventional ferries slow or cancel, and Quanta-LR's range margin keeps the longer crossings running.
signature_routes: Kaohsiung ↔ Magong (~75 nm open-strait link, Quanta-LR)
summary: Penghu is a scatter of roughly 90 islands in the Taiwan Strait, centred on Magong, that fills with visitors every summer for its beaches, basalt coastlines and the famous Penghu International Fireworks Festival. But it sits in one of the windiest seas in the region: the inter-island ferries and the mainland crossings are routinely slowed or cancelled by the strait's strong winds and the winter monsoon. Foiling above the chop turns that weather-fragility into a reliability premium — and a clean fleet fits a county pursuing UNESCO Biosphere recognition.
tagline: Taiwan's archipelago of ~90 islands in a windswept strait — a summer tourism magnet whose inter-island ferries are at the mercy of the weather.

use_cases.body: Foiling shuttles from Magong out to Jibei, Wangan and Cimei replace diesel ferries that cancel on windy days — turning the strait's weather-fragility into Penghu's reliability advantage during the summer rush.
use_cases.title: All-weather inter-island hopping

use_cases.body: A fast foiling link on the short ~25 nm Budai↔Magong crossing gives the mainland a frequent, smooth, all-electric gateway to the islands — flying above the chop that slows the conventional ferry.
use_cases.title: Chiayi/Budai gateway crossing

use_cases.body: A hybrid Quanta-LR service crosses the ~75 nm open strait from Kaohsiung in a fraction of the 4.5-hour ferry time, with the sea-state margin to keep running when conventional boats stay in port.
use_cases.title: Kaohsiung ↔ Magong fast link
